sources.used_for: work states, agent/app/user move tables, FIX_TO_WORK (mark_fixed) mapping and WORK_KEYS
PermissionError retry of os.replace (20 attempts, 50 ms)
set_state work/work_history rules, same-state update without history, claim cleared outside to_verify

adaptation: Rules are re-implemented in scripts/dispatch.py on immutable Two Hours plans and dispatch attempts; no Blurt store, MCP server, jobs or session runner is imported.
selected_changes: PR #18 (codex/blurt-task-receipts 56b53f3): mark_fixed state mapping, per-task UID, attempt ID, revision, work and work_history in dispatch-state.json; work-report, work-verify and ledger commands.
Explicit AGENT_MOVES / USER_DECISIONS / CLAIM_MOVE tables in scripts/dispatch.py, tested against the upstream lifecycle.json.
write_json retries os.replace only on PermissionError, 20 x 50 ms, then removes its temporary file.
work and every new work_history entry hold the 10 upstream WORK_KEYS plus source_thread and source_host.
A repeated report of the same state updates work in place without a history entry.
An accepted report_id sent again returns the earlier result before the failed-delivery check.
A report moving to a new state carries agent, and commit/pr unless the target is in_progress, from handed_off, in_progress or to_verify work, as upstream set_state does (items.py:844-852).

local_modifications.scripts/dispatch.py: Claim records by=app and the attempt authorization (manual: approval approved_at and approval_sha256; automatic: opt_in_id). Reports are rejected when delivery failed and accepted while it is sending. fsync and the run lock are kept; upstream write_text_atomic has neither.
local_modifications.tests/test_work_lifecycle.py: Two Hours tests; the deliberate differences from lifecycle.json are listed there with reasons.
local_modifications.tests/test_write_json_retry.py: Two Hours tests, including Windows-only tests with a reader holding the target open.

differences.reason: Two Hours has no new state; a task enters at handed_off when its approved batch is claimed.
A claim awaiting the user must be withdrawn with reopened before more work is reported.

differences.by: Claim is recorded as app in both authorization modes; reports as agent; work-verify as user.
differences.reason: Upstream does not let an agent move an item to handed_off; the user does not decide each task in automatic mode.

differences.same_as_upstream: claim, commit and pr are cleared; by is user; the previous work goes to work_history.
differences.reason: When the user sends a task back (to_verify -> todo), Two Hours keeps it bound to the session and attempt that receive the follow-up, and keeps the agent whose claim was rejected; upstream set_state carries nothing into todo (items.py:844-852).

differences.old_runs: Run files written before this change are read as they are: claim work may be null, verified work may have 4 keys and the attempt has no authorization. They are not migrated.
differences.reason: Run files are local per-run records; rewriting them would change already-recorded history.

not_imported: Blurt store, project index, ULID item UIDs (PR #18 uses a recomputable sha256 of plan, batch and task IDs), MCP server, jobs, session runner, new/discarded states and user actions other than done/wontfix/todo on to_verify.
